questions.question: Define capital, assets and liabilities and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Capital: money/resources the owner contributes to the business, e.g. R3 000 from savings. Assets: items of value the business owns, e.g. cash, equipment, vehicles, stock, debtors. Liabilities: amounts the business owes to outsiders, e.g. a loan, creditors.

questions.question: A business earns sales of R8 500 and pays rent R2 000, wages R3 000 and electricity R700. Calculate the profit and explain whether buying a new fridge for R4 000 is an expense.
questions.expected_answer: Expenses = R2 000 + R3 000 + R700 = R5 700. Profit = R8 500 − R5 700 = R2 800. The fridge is not an expense; it is an asset (equipment) because the business owns it and will use it for a long time.

questions.question: Name two things that increase and two things that decrease owner's equity.
questions.expected_answer: Increase: capital contributions, profit (income). Decrease: drawings, losses (expenses).
